findings.text: blocking (outside this node's declared write paths): the node renamed the remeasure receipt's count keys (at_or_below_benchmark_registered_1e_5 -> at_or_below_registered_residual_tolerance, at_or_below_shipped_hard_coded_1e_6 -> at_or_below_gate_residual_tolerance) but the reader benchmarks/derived_criterion_family.py:262 and :364 still indexes the two retired names from that receipt. The banked receipt docs/figures/diiid-forward-onboarding/repaired-solve-five-frame-remeasure.json still carries the retired names (bytes unchanged by the node), so the gate passes today; but that file is the benchmark's own DEFAULT_OUTPUT sibling (DEFAULT_OUTPUT) and regenerating it makes derived_criterion_family.py raise KeyError. The producer schema was changed without updating its consumer.

follow-on: the goal the node landed against (nova:diiid-forward-onboarding section 11: 'the remeasure benchmark still labels its record keys with the retired 1e-6') is achieved in the producer code but not in the artifact consumers actually read: the banked receipt still labels every frame with meets_shipped_hard_coded_1e_6 / at_or_below_shipped_hard_coded_1e_6 and the counts with the retired names. The node left the bank bytes and digest unchanged (documented in its manifest). No test asserts the bank is free of the retired labels, so the goal is only half-landed.

follow-on: the new test calls the helper _residual_tolerance_record directly with hand-passed tolerances and asserts the returned keys; it never exercises _solve_frame or run, so a regression that stopped run() from emitting the tolerance fields (or that reassigned GATE_RESIDUAL_BOUND back to 1.0e-6) would not redden it. The mutation the node used (a 1e_6 key suffix) is caught, but caller-path coverage is absent.
